# Benchmark results

The tables below compare tsrs, TypeScript 7 (tsgo) and `bun check` on seventeen projects. CI updates them on each
benchmark publish. The default-settings table runs each compiler at its own checker count (tsgo 4, tsrs up to one per
core); the `--checkers` 4, 8 and 16 tables run both at the same count. See [the methodology](README.md) for
the commands, pinned projects, hardware and measurement details, and [all recorded runs](results/) for other thread
counts and instruction counts.

## Benchmark: tsrs vs tsgo 7.0.2 vs bun check

Time and peak memory to type-check each project (`-p <project> --noEmit`) on Depot CI `depot-ubuntu-24.04-16` (16 vCPU, 63 GB RAM, Linux x86_64, AMD EPYC 9R45 96-Core Processor). Median of 10 interleaved runs (3 for tsgo).

- **tsrs**: commit `9ef0a57762d4`, PGO-optimized `dist` build, built like the npm release binaries.
- **tsgo**: npm `typescript@7.0.2`, the official Go compiler. tsrs ports a later 7.1-dev commit (`b85298b6`).
- **bun check**: Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+5f5799ed1.

Projects: vscode, xstate-main, webpack, mui-docs, Compiler, Compiler-Unions are from [microsoft/typescript-benchmarking](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-benchmarking), the suite the TypeScript team benchmarks tsgo on; the other 11 are large open-source applications.

### Default settings on 16 vCPUs

No thread flags: tsgo runs 4 checker threads; tsrs runs 16 (its default: all cores up to 16, then half the cores, at most 32; fewer on small projects); bun check runs one thread per core.

### Watch mode (vscode)

`--watch -p src --noEmit`, no thread flags, on Depot CI `depot-ubuntu-24.04-8` (8 vCPU, 31 GB RAM, Linux x86_64, AMD EPYC 9R45 96-Core Processor). Edits go to `src/vs/base/test/common/strings.test.ts`, a file nothing imports; an edit's time runs from the write to the cycle's report. Median of 5 (tsgo 3) sessions; the repeat edit is the median of 5 edits per session. bun check has no watch mode.

| step | tsgo | tsrs | tsrs vs tsgo |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| initial build | 10.51 s | 1.67 s | 6.28x faster |
| first comment edit | 2.58 s | 31 ms | 83.16x faster |
| repeat comment edit | 1.09 s | 28 ms | 38.79x faster |
| type error in a leaf file | 1.53 s | 30 ms | 51.03x faster |
| peak RSS | 12.09 GiB | 2.47 GiB | 4.89x less |
| RSS after the edits | 6.13 GiB | 1.39 GiB | 4.40x less |


Shared CI machines vary by a few percent between runs of the same code; the single-threaded instruction counts in `bench/results/` are the exact measure. Date: 2026-10-16 06:30 UTC. tsrs commit: `9ef0a57762d4`. Method: [benchmark methodology](https://github.com/maschwenk/tsrs/blob/main/bench/README.md).

## README chart

The [chart](large-projects.svg) plots TypeScript 7 against tsrs on VS Code, T3 Code and MUI docs from the latest
`--checkers` 4, 8 and 16 results above, both compilers at the same count on the 16-vCPU machine. Each project is a line
through a point per thread count: up is TypeScript 7's wall time over tsrs's, right is its peak memory over tsrs's,
and both axes start at 1x, the same as TypeScript 7. CI redraws it with the summary tables. Ratios use unrounded
medians. The SVG description lists the times and memory behind every point; its metadata records the measured commit,
date and modes.

## Historical comparison on 64 vCPUs

On 2026-10-07, type-checking vscode (10,427 files) on a 64-core Linux machine, each tool with its default settings, averaged over 20
runs ([source](results/compare/2026-10-07-ae33f10b1b8b-64t.md)):

| | time | peak memory |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| tsc 7 (tsgo 7.0.2) | 9.79 s | 7.52 GiB |
| `bun check` (Bun 1.4.3 canary) | 0.87 s | 2.86 GiB |
| **tsrs** | **0.53 s** | **2.64 GiB** |

### Against bun check at equal thread counts

The tools pick different thread counts by default, so here each one gets the same number (vscode, 64-core machine, 20
runs each):

| threads | tsgo 7.0.2 | tsrs | `bun check` |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 9.75 s, 7.43 GiB | 2.43 s, 1.83 GiB | 4.57 s, 1.46 GiB |
| 8 | 6.13 s, 7.99 GiB | 1.35 s, 1.97 GiB | 2.47 s, 1.60 GiB |
| 16 | 4.54 s, 8.67 GiB | 0.81 s, 2.13 GiB | 1.49 s, 1.85 GiB |
| 64 | 4.01 s, 11.58 GiB | 0.44 s, 3.06 GiB | 0.87 s, 2.86 GiB |

tsrs is about 1.9x faster at every thread count; tsrs uses 7-25% more memory. `bun check` follows TypeScript
7.0 and tsrs follows 7.1-dev, so their error counts can differ slightly; each matches its own reference exactly.

[Benchmark methodology](README.md) explains how everything is measured and how to rerun it. The published numbers
use the PGO-optimized release build, which is 7-14% faster than a plain `cargo build --release`.
